output.summary: A palm native to southwestern South America and restricted to a small area of central Chile. It is among the most massive palms, with an exceptionally thick trunk. Its edible seeds are widely eaten as Coquito nuts, while its sap is made into wine or syrup by methods now restricted under legal protection.
output.edibilityNote: Seeds are widely eaten as Coquito nuts; sap makes palm wine and syrup, although harvesting it by felling trees is legally restricted.
